before.name: payloadLength
before.meaning: FFD40 for the one 1 MiB fixture EXP-077 drove, which is size - 0x280 - 0x40. ONE SIZE WAS TESTED THE RELATION IS STATIC: the arena initialiser passes usableBytes - 0x40 to the header constructor 0036A490, which stores it here at 0036A50F, and 0x40 is this type's own size.
before.evidence: EXP-077 (ASTRA) establishes the initial free block at backing+0x280 with word FF12 and a dword payload length at +0x18. EXP-078 (ASTRA) runs seven allocation cases with NO callee stubs and identifies the neighbour links at +0x0C/+0x10 as the failing path, distinct from the free-list links at +0x04/+0x08. Re-read by OPUS from the unlinker 0036C9D0: 0036CA60 call 0020E600 decodes a neighbour reference, 0036CA75 mov [rsi+0xc],eax and 0036CA8A mov [rdi+0x10],eax store the re-encoded pair THROUGH THAT DECODED POINTER, and 0036CA92/0036CA99 tag the header word 0xFF99 on unlink. || THE RELATION TO THE ARENA'S usableBytes IS STATIC, NOT FITTED - 2026-09-21 (OPUS). The arena initialiser reads +0x5C back at 00369FC7, subtracts 0x40 at 00369FD0 and passes the result as the third argument to the header constructor 0036A490, which stores it here at 0036A50F (`mov dword ptr [rbx + 0x18], esi`). So payloadLength = usableBytes - 0x40 BY CONSTRUCTION, and 0x40 is exactly this type's declared size - the header consumes the first 0x40 bytes of the span it describes. The 0xFFD40 the one fixture produced is 0xFFD80 - 0x40, which the arithmetic now explains rather than merely agreeing with. exe 73461d0896204b1c259c52f61aef4efbc95a2ffc388cadb36493d5d1d89721f8

before.allocation_site: IMAGE 022D7FD0 - fifteen records of 0xA8 in .bss. The record itself is never allocated; the BACKING it points at comes through an imported malloc path and is not part of this record.
before.ctor: 00369D30 initializer (707 B); its block-header writer is 0036A490 (215 B)
before.evidence: EXP-077 (ASTRA, 2026-09-12) executed the initializer 00369D30 as shipped bytes under Unicorn and checked the record's fields individually at THREE backing addresses - 40010000, 80010000 and 100010000 - so the field-to-backing relationship holds across a range rather than for one fixture. Re-verified by OPUS against the image before use: the body sha256 16466da3... matches, and the id bound at 00369D47 is cmp esi,0xE / ja, UNSIGNED, which is what rejects the negative id that 00369D3B sign-extended. The 0xA8 stride and the 022D7FD0 base are also read by 0036BC60, which splits linked free blocks across fifteen such records. || ALLOCATOR-SIDE EVIDENCE, 2026-09-20 (OPUS), and a census caveat this row should carry. 0036BC60 reaches a record with 'lea rax, [022D7FD0] ; imul rbx, rcx, 0xa8 ; add rbx, rax' (0036BCA9-0036BCBE) after bounding the id with 'cmp ecx, 0xE ; ja', which re-confirms base, stride and count from the allocation side as well as the initialiser side. It also sets byte +0x02 to 1 on entry (0036BCC5) and rounds every request up to a multiple of 0x40 (0036BC92-0036BC9D) - the same 0x40 as the block header, so payload and header share one granularity. THE CAVEAT: a fixed-address census of this table MISSES 0036BC60 completely. An `xor ebx, ebx` on the out-of-range error arm sits between the base computation and its uses in linear order, so the base is killed before the reads. That is blind spot 9 in _index/ABSENCE-CLAIM-GATE.md, found here; static_array_census.py now reports such boundaries in LAST_POSTJMP_KILLS. Measured effect on this table: 41 accesses versus 57 under the alternative reading, and the SAME 26 offsets either way. || EXP-127 DOES NOT LICENSE A PROMOTION OF THIS TYPE, 2026-09-21 (OPUS), consuming ASTRA-RETURN-OPUS-EXP127-INSTRUMENT-BOUNDARY. RECORDED AS A FORWARD GUARD, NOT A CORRECTION - nothing on this type or any other in the store cites EXP-127, checked by searching both types.tsv and fields.tsv for it, so no present claim moves. THE RISK ASTRA NAMES IS A FUTURE PROMOTION and this cell is where it would happen. THE BOUNDARY: EXP-127's raw review is ACCEPT-WITH-NARROWING and its session is marked INVALID_POST_TRACE. An accepted audit and a successful API return are NOT a healthy session, and neither is evidence about arena semantics. A new exact-source control demonstrates a foreign-step dispatch defect, and all 5,658 saved step events still match configured ownership in the recorded fields - so the defect is demonstrated and NO CAUSAL LINK to the fatal dialog is established. One extra 003E3C7A event occurs during cleanup outside the 2,113 logged pairs and is unexplained. WHAT THIS TYPE ACTUALLY RESTS ON, and it is a different and stronger class: EXP-077 and EXP-078 executed the initializer 00369D30 as SHIPPED BYTES under Unicorn with no callee stubs, checking the record's fields at three separate backing addresses. That is isolated original-code execution, which does not depend on any session being healthy. The one live citation on this type is EXP-079's records for arenas 2-14, which is a different experiment from EXP-127 and is not implicated by this return. SO THE RULE FOR ANYONE PROMOTING THIS TYPE LATER: EXP-127 may not be cited as evidence that an arena was initialised, that animation state was live, or that a session was healthy. Native qualification and a healthy FF12 session are both still absent.
